What happens when a man gets transported into a foreign world filled with magic?

Will his knowledge in hardware technology help him out after he discovers its correlation to the words of power?

How will he fit in with the other noble houses as the lowly 4th son?

How will his story play out in a world where skills and stats equal power and status?

Not a bad story put to death by the author

Reviewed at: Chapter 504 – Gliding Rescue.
by Necrozma Saturday, November 23, 2024 10:56:00 PM

The story had an unusual set up - a standard transport to another world, but the main character decides to leave home so that no one can mess with him.
Up to about 200 chapters I read with pleasure, but then the whole story began to deteriorate, and in the end by chapter 500 we were left with low quality rubbish instead of a plot, a discarded system, and a complete disregard for the essence of the rune smith.
The story was dynamic until mcha decided to build a family. This quickly began to drag on for dozens of boring tedious chapters where the plot stood still, where nothing happened.
The dialogues for the most part made no sense, most of the text in the chapters referenced themselves in the same way.
Most of the characters are just bad or stupid, most of all mch.
His decisions are often questionable at best and downright stupid at worst.
The laws of the world almost never work. The system is inarticulate.
For some reason, the concept of the rune smith is relegated to the background and only mentioned as a means to an end.
The protagonist does literally nothing, because of the author creating situations where he has to get out of his comfort zone, because of this it seems like the whole world works only to entertain the protagonist so he doesn't get bored.
Events that can be told in a couple of chapters sometimes stretch for 10-20-30 chapters.
At chapter 505 I stop reading.

Great story, feels a bit weird.

Reviewed at: Chapter 319– Back Home.
by StrangestQuark Friday, April 7, 2023 9:27:54 AM

The story is interesting and well paced, the enemies feel appropriately OP at the beginning and the grind of levelling up is written very well.

The system is mostly done in a very casual way, not dominating the story as some of the LitRPG are wont to do and a lot of my usual issues with the genre are taken care of with good pacing and minimal interaction with the system.

The grammar/phrasing is decent, unless you are especially sensitive to it you probably won't have any issues with it.

The characters are usually interesting enough to remember even if they are only taking part of a small part of the story, which is really the only thing you can ask for in side characters. The main cast though feels a bit shallow for main characters, I highly doubt anyone will fall in love with their personality. 

That being said, as all stories this one has a few flaws too of course, the MC is very static and the story started to stick nearly entirely to one, not particularly important, location making it feel like the plot is not really moving forward despite logically knowing that it does.

All things considered, probably not the GOAT of LitRPG but a very good story to pick up if you want to pick up something new.

Overall

Cardboard Characters

Reviewed at: Chapter 247 – Foxy.
by Natasha Velkirk (Zach or Zach) Sunday, February 26, 2023 1:30:08 AM

Most of the other reviews I saw said that there were good concepts, and not so great execution.

I would somewhat disagree. The concept, and how the mainstay are executed are excellent. The Runesmithing, that is. I can remember liking almost every part that was the character just tinkering, or testing out his new weapons against dangerous creatures.

I remember that part of the story as genuinely fantastic.

The problem is that all the characters other than the MC were flat boring tropes. Serious wife, airhead who's secretly badass, lecher but a hard worker, battle maniac who gets reined in by a character of theopposite gender (iirc sibling in this case), and it has been awhile, but this is pretty much all I can remember from the characters. The main character was slightly more nuanced, but only slightly. He just randomly gets married, randomly gets and assistant, randomly gets friends who act similar to a found family, it's all very typical and played out.

Now tropes are.tropes for a reason, they tend to be at least somewhat entertaining, and easy to twist into something different, but when coupled with an at times rough writing style, and a story that seems averse to being particularly interesting in any way other than the Runesmithing, it just gets boring. It's a story you've already seen all the components of, once again, other than the Runesmithing. It's been, I think a year, since I read this, but one thing aticks in my head. The main character just crafting, attempting to circumvent obstacles, that sort of thing.

The combat I remember being fairly well done if not exceptional, but there felt like enough room to grow into something more.with time. The problem is that the story feels tied down to being a generic and uninspired shounen. It feels very anime inspired, but without the characters that make me interested in seeing the results of interesting concepts at play. I'm just uninterested in reading the story any further.

I don't really dislike it. But it doesn't produce any real enjoyment for me either. That bothers me, and I've thought of this story a few times since I stopped reading.

To be honest, I just wish it was a little bit better, or a little bit worse. At least then I could laugh at its silliness, enjoy what is good, but instead it just feels like a husk. A story that promises to hold your interest, but simply lacks any real substance, despite it's clear potential.

It is, in one simple word....

Disappointing.

Starts off great then steadily goes downhill

Reviewed at: Chapter 560 – Months Later.
by deliver Sunday, August 31, 2025 4:10:49 PM

The reviws that you can find for this novel differ a lot and usually the scores range between barely 3 and 5 stars for a reason. Both scores are right in a way because this work is arguably five stars material at the start then slowly goes downhill after the Main Character settles down between chapters 150-200 until the novel becomes three stars material at most.

I think 3.5 is a fair score all things considered, because while I agree that it has worsened a lot, to the point that it is difficult for me to continue, I cannot forget how much I liked the first parts of this work, even with their pacing limitations. It is a pity because a novel that could have been great feels like a missed opportunity. If you are looking for something good you have got a couple hundred chapters here then I suggest leaving it as soon as you feel like it.
